history.summary: NON-TEMPLE RECORD (keep-or-drop decision needed): Chakratirtha is the sacred circular spring-fed kund at the centre of Naimisharanya, not a temple building. Per tradition, Lord Vishnu released his Sudarshan Chakra to show the sages the best place for meditation, and where it fell (in another version, Lord Brahma's Manomaya Chakra cracked the earth) the 'bottomless' sweet-water spring rose - giving Naimisharanya its name ('nemi' = the wheel's outer rim). A local legend says the British tried to disprove the bottomless-spring claim by dropping a 3,300-foot cable without hitting bottom. It is the spiritual heart of the tirtha: pilgrims bathe here to cleanse sins before visiting Lalita Devi, Hanuman Garhi and the other temples. CSV TOWN NOTE: the municipal town is Misrikh-cum-Neemsar (Sitapur district); 'Naimisharanya' is the pilgrimage-town name. Coordinates are the Naimisharanya town centre - approximate (verify). name: Chakratirtha
town_description: Naimisharanya is an ancient forest-pilgrimage town in Sitapur district, Uttar Pradesh, on the left bank of the Gomati river, about 90-100 km from Lucknow. One of the most sacred Hindu tirthas, it is associated with the 88,000 rishis who meditated here, the recitation of the Puranas by Suta to Shaunaka, and major temples including Lalita Devi (Shakti Peetha) and Hanuman Garhi.
